subject: Reserved pool throughput safeguards & token-rate addendum — Renewal discussion
messages:
From: Dana Park <dana.park@acme-ai.com>
To: Connor O'Brien <connor_obrien@redwood.com>
Cc: Evan Li <evan.li@acme-ai.com>
Date: Mon, 12 Jul 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Renewal: reserved pool + additional GPUs — token-rate expectations

Connor —

As we discussed in the renewal call last week, ACME is planning to expand our dedicated pool for Q4. We are targeting a reserved top-up of +8 GPUs (A100 class), and need clear throughput assurances so our engineering team can size front-end rate limits. Specifically, we want an addendum that ties Reserved Pool capacity to a token-rate guarantee (tokens/sec sustained) rather than just GPUs — we care about steady-state request-level guarantees.

Can you send a proposed addendum that: 1) maps the +8 GPUs to an expected sustained tokens/sec, 2) describes burst handling and a short fallback path if we exceed sustained limits, and 3) spells out service credits if you miss the SLO over a monthly rolling window?

We also attached our capacity planning sheet for your reference.

Thanks,
Dana Park
Head of Platform Integrations
ACME AI

Attachments: capacity_topup_sheet_acme_q3.xlsx
From: Connor O'Brien <connor_obrien@redwood.com>
To: Dana Park <dana.park@acme-ai.com>
Cc: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 12 Jul 2027 11:00:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Renewal: reserved pool + additional GPUs — token-rate expectations

Dana —

Thanks for the clear ask and the spreadsheet — helpful. Attached is a first-pass addendum (redwood_reserved_pool_addendum_draft_v3.pdf) that: 1) converts the proposed +8 A100s to a conservative sustained tokens/sec target (we show a baseline and a 95th-percentile expected rate), 2) defines a 2-tier burst policy (short bursts up to 150% sustained with ephemeral burst credits, longer bursts are routed to best-effort hosts), and 3) proposes a service credit schedule tied to monthly rolling SLO attainment (partial credits that scale with outage magnitude, capped at 30% of the monthly reservation fee).

High level clarifications included in the doc:
- Measurement: uptime and token-rate attainment measured at the dedicated pool level, 5-minute rolling windows aggregated into daily availability.
- Fallback: automatic regional fallback to compatible model variants when sustained tokens/sec is exceeded and no burst credits remain. We limit fallbacks to preserve correctness and will only route to variants that have been validated by your team.
- Escalation: automated alerting to both teams and a 2-hour remediation SLA for production-impact events.

Marissa — tagging you for legal-level SLO language and whether the cap on credits is acceptable. Neha — flagging for whether the monitoring link and math in Appendix B (tokens_to_tps_modeling.csv) match our internal metering.

Connor
Director, Customer Solutions
Redwood Inference

Attachments: redwood_reserved_pool_addendum_draft_v3.pdf; tokens_to_tps_modeling.csv
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Connor O'Brien <connor_obrien@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 12 Jul 2027 14:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Fwd: Draft addendum — suggested SLO language

Quick internal thread before we reply to ACME with a marked-up doc. Notes: 

1) Service credit schedule — I recommend we keep the cap at 30% but change the trigger windows: use a 7-day sustained shortfall window for the higher credit band rather than a single monthly event to avoid gaming. Also add a small "measurement uncertainty" buffer (1%) to account for sampling differences.

2) Burst policy — be explicit that burst credits are finite and consumed on a per-pool basis; include an option to purchase an "extended burst" bucket as part of the renewal (this is an upsell). Put pricing in Appendix C.

3) Fallbacks — do not commit to routing >10% of traffic to fallback variants without prior sign-off. Instead, state we will do a 24-hour canary for any fallback variant and provide fall-forward metrics.

4) Monitoring / SLI links — ensure we expose the metric name and the Grafana dashboards (we currently have a private link for customers). Asking Neha to confirm the exact metric IDs used for tokens/sec and the aggregation window.

If all agree I will prepare a marked-up PDF to return to Dana.

- Marissa
Sr. Counsel, Contracts & Renewals
Redwood Inference
From: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Connor O'Brien <connor_obrien@redwood.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 13 Jul 2027 09:22:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Draft addendum — suggested SLO language

Marissa —

Confirmed: tokens/sec SLI is "dedicated_pool.tokens_per_second.sustained" aggregated in 5-minute windows and reported as a 95th percentile on a rolling 30-day basis for invoicing/SLOs. We can include a 1% instrumentation buffer as you suggested. Appendix B (tokens_to_tps_modeling.csv) matches our internal throughput model but note: mapping tokens to user requests depends heavily on avg prompt length; we added sample columns showing ranges for 16-token prompts up to 1024-token contexts.

On burst purchase: finance okayed an "extended burst" SKU that can be added at renewal; product will need to enable quota enforcement. I'll include the SKU ID in the marked-up doc.

I'll update the addendum with metric names, retention, and the Grafana link (we'll provide a shared read-only dashboard).

- Neha
Head of Platform Observability
Redwood Inference
From: Dana Park <dana.park@acme-ai.com>
To: Connor O'Brien <connor_obrien@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Evan Li <evan.li@acme-ai.com>, Procurement <procurement@acme-ai.com>
Date: Thu, 14 Jul 2027 16:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Renewal: reserved pool + additional GPUs — token-rate expectations

Connor / Marissa —

Thanks for the fast turn-around and the detailed notes. Overall this looks good; a few items before legal signs: 

- Please change the fallback cap from 10% to 15% for our initial 60-day ramp period. After 60 days we can revert to 10%.
- On credits: acceptable as long as the 7-day shortfall trigger is spelled out and we get visibility into the raw measurement windows (we need to reconcile with our logs during the first billing cycle).
- We are interested in purchasing the extended burst bucket for Q4; please include the SKU and a pro-rated price for the remainder of the term.

If you can return a redlined PDF with these three updates (fallback cap during ramp, explicit 7-day trigger language, extended burst SKU/pricing) we will route to legal and procurement for signature.

Best,
Dana
Head of Platform Integrations
ACME AI

Attachments: none
